text:
incident-bot: PagerDuty: PROD-REDIS-MAXCLIENTS fired (severity: high) - service: redis-cluster-prod - triggered by metric maxclients >= 10000
pagerduty: Incident PROD-REDIS-MAXCLIENTS created and escalated to on-call schedule (page sent)
devon: acked. i'm on it. pulling up dashboards nowsara: thanks. initial alerts show maxclients spike across both redis-primary pods, redises at ~98% of maxclients and latency climbing >200ms
matt: any correlating DB errors? could be connection storm from API layer
devon: digging logs from api-prod-1/2: lots of socket timeouts and reconnect loops, repeated 502s. client apps trying to open new conns instead of reusing pool
sara: running `redis-cli -h redis-primary-0 INFO clients` gives: connected_clients: 4923
devon: primary-0 and primary-1 showing similar. maxclients=5000 configured on both -> that's the issue, we're at the cap
lia: queued requests on the application side are starting to backpressure. Customer-facing latency climbing to 5-10s for some writes, error rate +5% in last 5m
matt: can we temporary bump maxclients? that's risky but fastest mitigation. Or scale redis replicas?
sara: options: 1) increase maxclients and restart pods (downtime for connections?) 2) scale up nodes (if we're on k8s, add nodePool) 3) throttle API clients via feature-flag or rate-limit (safer)
devon: doing quick audit - which services are creating the most connections? running `ss -ntp | grep redis | awk '{print $5}' | cut -d: -f1 | sort | uniq -c | sort -nr` on primary-0
devon: top offenders: api-worker-7 (1200 conns), transformer-3 (900), migration-job-2 (700), unknown 192.168.40.99 (450)
lia: migration-job-2 is a scheduled shard-cleanup, it shouldn't be running now. someone started a manual job?
matt: that IP 192.168.40.99 is the pgbouncer host for analytics — looks like analytics is hitting redis for some counters; we should throttle that
pagerduty: Reminder: if incident exceeds 30m, consider paged escalation to SRE lead
sara: immediate plan: 1) ask dev teams to stop non-critical jobs (lia please msg infra teams) 2) put an app-level circuit-breaker on transformer & analytics 3) temporarily increase maxclients to 8000 on both primaries and monitor
devon: i'll run the config bump with zero-downtime if possible. applying `sed` change to redis.conf and rolling restart with one pod at a time.
lia: pinging analytics, ops, and data-platform in #support now: "urgent: stop ad-hoc analytics jobs, we're at redis maxclients, please back off until cleared" :rotating_light:
analytics-team (in #support): acknowledged, killing current ad-hoc query processes, will hold new runs
matt: i'll coordinate with infra; if we need capacity fast, we can spin an extra replica group (add shards) but that requires rebalancing; prefer config bump first
sara: devon, please do the config bump on primary-1 first (less traffic) and watch for connection churn
devon: starting on primary-1 now. command: `kubectl exec -it redis-primary-1 -- bash -c "sed -i 's/maxclients 5000/maxclients 8000/' /data/redis/redis.conf && redis-cli -h 10.0.2.17 CONFIG REWRITE"`
devon: CONFIG REWRITE succeeded on primary-1. triggering rolling restart: `kubectl rollout restart statefulset/redis-primary -n prod --field-selector metadata.name=redis-primary-1`
sara: monitor client reconnects. if we see large reconnect storms, might flip to rolling restart slower
devon: primary-1 back up. connected_clients: 5210 -> ok so bump helped there
lia: customer-impact update: Partial impact to write-heavy endpoints. We have ~12% of production requests experiencing >3s latency; top affected customers: alpha-corp and beta-startup (IDs masked) - support notified
matt: checking primary-0 next. I'll coordinate to avoid both pods restarting concurrently
devon: doing primary-0 now, same steps
devon: primary-0 back up. connected_clients: 6100 -> above our previous max but below new limit 8000. latency dropping to ~80-120ms
sara: good. next: enforce app-side pooling. lia, please get ops to push an emergency feature flag to reduce concurrency from 50 -> 10 for transformer and api-worker pools
lia: on it. feature-flag rollout started via infra-ops: `ffctl set transformer.max_concurrency 10 --env prod --override`
pagerduty: paging note: incident acknowledged by devon; no escalation yet
analytics-team: removed long-running queries and rate limited ETL, analytics now at 5% of prior connection rate
sara: long-term action items (postmortem): - review service connection pooling defaults - add metrics for connections per service - implement automatic client-side backpressure / token bucket - evaluate raising maxclients permanently or sharding session state
matt: also check pgbouncer misconfigs; we saw that pgbouncer host making many redis calls — that pattern is odd
devon: will open a follow-up ticket for pgbouncer -> redis dependency mapping
lia: support update: support pings sent to affected accounts with note: "Transient write latency; mitigations applied; monitoring closely"
sara: closing loop: system metrics stable for 10m, error rate back to baseline, latency improving. I'll keep monitors on for 30m and then close the PD incident if stable
devon: thanks team. leaving handoff notes for night oncall in #eng-oncall: "watch redis connected_clients and api-worker connection churn; if >75% of new max for 10m, escalate to SRE lead"
pagerduty: Incident PROD-REDIS-MAXCLIENTS status: monitoring (acknowledged)
incident-bot: Incident note added by sara: "temporary maxclients bump + app-side throttles; investigating root cause and follow-ups"
sara: last: thanks all. follow-ups: postmortem owner: devon, timeline draft by EOD tomorrow.
